content_voiceover: This is the ADMIRAL trial, the pivotal phase three study that got gilteritinib approved for relapsed or refractory FLT3-mutated AML, and it's a very commonly tested trial. Patients with R/R FLT3-mutated AML were randomized to gilteritinib at one hundred twenty milligrams daily, two hundred forty-seven patients, versus investigator's choice salvage chemotherapy, one hundred twenty-four patients. The Kaplan-Meier curve shows clear separation favoring gilteritinib throughout follow-up. Median overall survival was nine point three months with gilteritinib compared to five point six months with salvage chemotherapy, a hazard ratio of zero point six three seven, highly significant at p equals zero point zero zero zero seven. Twelve-month overall survival rates reinforce this, thirty-seven percent alive at one year with gilteritinib versus only seventeen percent with chemotherapy. This is the trial that established single-agent FLT3 inhibition as superior to conventional salvage chemotherapy in relapsed FLT3-mutated AML, and it's why gilteritinib became the standard salvage option for this population.

Median OS, nine point three months versus five point six months

keypoint_voiceover: ADMIRAL established gilteritinib as superior to salvage chemotherapy in relapsed FLT3-mutated AML, with median overall survival of nine point three months versus five point six months, and roughly double the one-year survival rate.
